meta.description: Two rating experiments on English antonymic adjectives under negation, Experiment 1 on relative adjectives and Experiment 2 on absolute ones, each with eight items. An item is a context in which a speaker with full knowledge makes eight statements, crossing the evaluative polarity of the adjective (positive or negative), its scalar strength (weak or strong) and the presence of negation; participants saw the eight statements concurrently and rated each individual on a 1-5 scale from the negative strong adjective to the positive strong one. The ratings were analysed with cumulative link mixed models with treatment-coded Negation (negated as the reference level) and Scalar Strength, and sum-coded Evaluative Polarity; a significant effect of Negation indicates an asymmetric interpretation of the positive and negative adjectives under negation at the reference level of Scalar Strength. The rating proportions of the figures are not printed and are not recorded.
